# CrowdStrike puts Guardian kill switch at gateway; endpoint follows


By OpenTools Team


The November 3 update separates gateway control, operating‑system inspection support and planned Fiddler observability.


##


Gateway first


Guardian has been generally available since September. CrowdStrike says its included AI Gateway is now generally available, routing prompts and responses through centralized policy inspection. The new kill switch starts there; endpoint support is coming soon. Buyers should distinguish that gateway release from terminating a locally running process.[CrowdStrike announcement](https://crowdstrike.gcs-web.com/news-releases/news-release-details/crowdstrike-delivers-ai-security-and-safety-enterprise)


##


Separate inspection and acquisition stages


Endpoint network inspection is generally available on Windows; Mac is early access. It connects network communication with endpoint activity, according to CrowdStrike. Fiddler observability depends on a planned acquisition and integration. These stages identify which capability to request in a demonstration; the announcement supplies no independent efficacy test.[CrowdStrike announcement](https://crowdstrike.gcs-web.com/news-releases/news-release-details/crowdstrike-delivers-ai-security-and-safety-enterprise)


CrowdStrike office sign in Sunnyvale, October 2024; archive context, not Guardian controls or a product test.
